text:
incident-bot: CRITICAL - High tail token latency spike detected on hosted inference pool 'eu-central-1-a' starting ~10:45 UTC. Alerting on-call.

Maria Chen: paging @oncall - I'm seeing p95 token-latency jump from 120ms -> 950ms for gptx-8k-continuous. Error rates fine, but a lot of in-flight seq lengths shot up.

Alex Patel: thanks - grabbing the runbook. Are we sure this is latency and not KV cache eviction thrash?

Maria Chen: KV hits look stable in metrics, cache size steady. Throughput dropped too. There are a lot of large requests with early-flush disabled after last runtime deploy.

Sam R: I'm oncall. I'm seeing continuous_batch_window_ms defaulted to 40ms in the new deploy. Old value was 10ms. That would increase aggregation and increase tail.

Jordan L: ugh, that lines up with the deploy-bot note: deploy-bot: Deployed runtime v2.14.7 to eu-central-1-a (2024-07-12 10:42 UTC) with adaptive_batching and continuous_window bump.

Kevin O: Confirmed - the rollout configured continuous_window_ms=40 for easier throughput. We likely under-estimated tail impact.

Sam R: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert continuous_window_ms to 10ms on the host pool OR 2) enable per-route short-window override for latency-sensitive routes + apply emergency rate limits for large-seq customers. Which is faster?

Maria Chen: Revert is straightforward but triggers another deploy. Short-window override can be applied via runtime feature flag and should be faster. I can push a flag change to target the gptx-8k model routes.

Alex Patel: while Maria prepares the flag, I'm going to temporarily lower max_batch_size on the pool to reduce queueing. That should reduce latency at cost of throughput.

Sam R: do both. Also open a protective quota for top 5 noisy tenants to limit long sequences for next 30m. Customer-impact aware: CS and Sales should be notified if we throttle.

Maria Chen: applying flag now: PATCH to runtime-control API:

```
PATCH /runtime-control/pools/eu-central-1-a/overrides
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model_filter": "gptx-8k*",
  "continuous_window_ms": 10,
  "adaptive_batching": true
}
```

Maria Chen: flag accepted. Should propagate to frontends in ~15s.

deploy-bot: feature-flag update applied to 17/20 hosts in pool eu-central-1-a.

Alex Patel: lowering pool max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 via CLI:

```
./adminctl set-pool-config --pool eu-central-1-a --max-batch-size 24
```

Alex Patel: command executed, pods restarting one-by-one. Early metrics look promising: p95 dropping to ~200ms on initial shards.

Sam R: I will push short-term rate-limit rules for routes hitting >500 token seqs. Using traffic-shaper:

```
traffic-shaper add-rule --pool eu-central-1-a --match "request.tokens > 500" --limit 30rps --duration 30m
```

Sam R: rule applied. We're also cutting burst allowances to 1.5x.

Maria Chen: CS-alert: @cs-team - we will throttle very long requests for ~30m in eu-central region to protect latency. ETA for full resolution ~45m.

Jordan L: monitoring logs: tail-latency correlates with backlog depth; batch sizes observed in logs spiked to 52-60 after the deploy. Good we've lowered max_batch_size.

Kevin O: quick customer-impact check: top noisy tenant (acct-847) shows 12% of requests were >500 tokens. They may see higher throttling/failures. @cs-team please prepare outbound note if they open a ticket.

Sam R: handoff - I'm active for next 30m then offshift. Maria, can you take lead on runbook steps and escalate if propagation stalls?

Maria Chen: taking lead. I'll watch until p95 < 250ms for 10 minutes across all hosts before we relax rate-limits.

Alex Patel: one more tuning we can do if needed: enable early-flush threshold lowering so batches flush at 12 tokens instead of waiting for max_batch_size. Quick config:

```
./adminctl set-runtime-param --name early_flush_tokens --value 12 --pool eu-central-1-a
```

Maria Chen: Noted. Leave as option if p95 doesn't stabilize after flag + batch-size change.

deploy-bot: runtime v2.14.7 rollback candidate prepared (config only) - requires approval to rollout.

Sam R: rollback is last resort because it affects many customers; prefer config overrides. If things don't improve in 20m we can approve rollback.

Maria Chen: metrics update (10:55 UTC): p95 190ms, p99 420ms on average across pool. Throughput down ~18% but acceptable.

Jordan L: logs show a small error pattern: "early_flush_threshold not set" noise when we applied the override - looks cosmetic. No functional error.

Sam R: good. Leave the traffic-shaper and reduced max_batch_size for now. I'll escalate to infra if we need more capacity or cross-region draining.

Maria Chen: as of 11:20 UTC p95 stable ~210ms for 15m window. Removing the tenant-specific quota for acct-999 which we throttled earlier.

Alex Patel: I'll keep the smaller max_batch_size until next deploy window and add a canary test that measures p95 for window changes.

Sam R: handoff note for the next oncall: monitor eu-central-1-a for 2h for regressions after deploy. Key signals: p95 token latency, avg batch size, queue depth, KV-hit ratio. If p95 creeps >300ms revert to 10ms window + consider early-flush.

Maria Chen: I'll post incident summary after we close. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Tickets: INC-2024-3247.

Maria Chen: Summary draft: mitigated latency spike caused by new continuous_batch_window default increase in runtime v2.14.7. Live mitigations: feature-flag override to restore 10ms for gptx-8k routes, reduce pool max_batch_size to 24, temporary rate-limits for long-sequence requests, optional early-flush knob held in reserve. No major customer outages; targeted throttling applied to a small set of heavy tenants. Follow-up: revert problematic default in config before next rollout and add a canary measuring p95 per-window-size.

Jordan L: adding post-incident action: add automated test in CI that simulates high long-seq traffic and asserts p95 < 300ms for new continuous_window settings.

Sam R: closing handoff. If anything reappears ping me directly.

Maria Chen: closing thread and filing postmortem in /incidents with links to runbook steps and exact CLI commands used.
